summary: Abandoned but not Forgotten is an interactive web platform developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge that transforms over 60 years of NASA's off-world hardware history into story-driven experiences for young explorers. Using authentic NASA mission data and imagery, we created a digital hub spotlighting more than 70 robotic explorers and over 200 tons of hardware resting on the Moon and Mars—such as Apollo descent stages, lunar rovers, retroreflectors, and Mars missions like Spirit, Opportunity, Viking, and InSight—across four engaging formats: clickable lunar "ghost rover" maps, first-person lander graphic novels, audio podcasts chronicling deep-space instrument finales, and playable 3D timelines. By turning dense technical archives into accessible, multi-sensory storytelling, the project directly addresses the challenge of making space science engaging for different learning styles, preserving these silent monuments as living time capsules that inspire STEM curiosity in the next generation.
details: Nasa Moon and Mars hardware history into fun, interactive stories for kids and teens. Using real NASA/JPL data and LROC Moon photos of 70+ retired spacecraft—like Apollo landers and Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity—we built clickable Moon maps, graphic novels from a lander's POV, short podcasts about their final days, and playable 3D timelines. We coded the web app with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, and Three.js, drew the comics in Figma, and edited the audio in Audacity. Our goal was to replace boring mission logs with creative, relatable stories across reading, listening, and playing so different learners can connect with real space science.
